turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Dave, come on through. Obs are done, blood pressure one thirty-two over eighty-four, heart rate seventy-six, temperature thirty-six point eight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, Jen, stick around in case I need you. Dave, Karen, grab a seat. What can I do for you?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, it's me lower back, doctor. Been sore.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is it an ache, or does it catch?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Dull ache, and it catches if I bend. I don't know, doctor, words aren't my strong suit.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's been groaning getting out of the ute. Proper weeks of it.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Where do you feel it?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Low, belt-line, more on the right side. Not between the shoulders.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain running down the leg?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Stays in the back, maybe a bit in the right bum. That's it.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has it been there?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): A few weeks. Or, well, actually, since the move. I don't know, doctor, I can't lock in a date.
[SEG0013] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The move was the start of March, so six weeks. He was lumping boxes the whole weekend.
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, call it six weeks then. I still couldn't tell you the first morning.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Righto, about six weeks, the actual day uncertain. I'll go through the serious features separately so we don't blur them.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any numbness, pins and needles, or weakness in the legs, or around the groin and saddle?

[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, last Tuesday I was stood on the concrete for hours and the right foot went pins and needles. It came good once I walked to the smoko room. I don't know if that counts, doctor. It's not there today, and I don't reckon the back did it.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sounds like the foot simply went to sleep. So is there numbness now, or a leg that's weak?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No numbness now, no weakness.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about the bladder, leaking, trouble starting, not feeling the urge?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): No, bladder's normal. No worries there.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight loss you weren't trying for?

[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I thought the belt was on a looser hole, but we've ditched takeaway while the kitchen's unpacked, and I haven't weighed myself. I don't think I've lost weight.
[SEG0024] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He hasn't. Same old jeans.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll record no unintentional weight loss. Any fever, chills, or night sweats?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever, no sweats. I get whacked after a shift, but that's just the warehouse, not illness.

[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Off topic, but my mum takes metformin for her diabetes, has done for years, and Dave's sister chews biotin gummies for her hair. I keep thinking he needs a supplement. Silly, probably.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Your mum's metformin and his sister's biotin aren't his medicines, so they stay off his list. A supplement won't sort mechanical pain. Dave, what are you actually using?

[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Panadol from the chemist. Two of the five hundred milligram tablets in the morning, and two more after work if the ache is up. If I'm okay I skip the arvo dose. I don't know, doctor, I just follow the box.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies, rashes, swelling with medicines?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Never had one. I don't know of any allergy.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me about the job.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Picker in a warehouse. Lifting cartons, some around twenty kilos, on my feet for an eight hour shift. Been doing it for years.
[SEG0034] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And we just moved to a rental in Footscray, so there were house boxes on top of that.

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's have a look. Bend forward. You halt around mid-thigh, and the right lower back muscles are tender. Straight leg raise is comfortable, no pain down the leg, and the feet are strong.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, the bend is rotten. Lying flat on the floor settles it, a hot shower helps, and the wheat bag at night.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Score out of ten when it's bad?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe a six. Quiet days are more like a three. It chops and changes.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): So, thinking it through out loud. No red flags for cauda equina, infection, or something sinister. My working impression is a mechanical low back strain related to the lifting, present for six weeks. I can't completely rule out a small disc irritation because it's lingered, but nothing on today's exam shows a trapped nerve, so that stays unlikely.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Gaz from work had a scan and a back op and he still can't lift. Am I heading there? I don't know, doctor.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't put you in Gaz's boat. No scan today. A plain X-ray won't earn its keep here, so I'm not ordering one. We might arrange an MRI if this hasn't settled in a fortnight.

[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stick with the Panadol, two five-hundred milligram tablets morning and again after work only when you need them. Don't start your sister's biotin or your mother-in-law's tablets. Cut back the heavy cartons if the boss allows, keep walking, stay out of bed all day. If you can't pass urine, if numbness comes and stays, or if you get a fever with much worse pain, get seen the same day, emergency for the bladder.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Right. So I just wait and see?
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back and see me in two weeks, Jen can book it, so I can recheck the movement. If it hasn't eased by then, that's when we might go ahead with the MRI.

symptoms.onset: around the house move at the start of March; exact morning unknown
symptoms.body_site: lower back along the belt line, more on the right, sometimes the right buttock
symptoms.relieving_factors: lying flat on the floor, hot shower, wheat bag at night

symptoms.name: pins and needles in the right foot
symptoms.onset: last Tuesday, after standing on concrete for hours

negative_findings.finding: current numbness in the legs or saddle area

clinical_assessment.basis: no red flags for cauda equina, infection, or a sinister cause, and examination without a trapped nerve
pain has lingered for six weeks, but examination shows no trapped nerve

procedures_and_investigations.indication: if the back pain has not settled in a fortnight

clinical_actions.description: Continue Panadol, two 500 mg tablets in the morning and two after work only when needed
Do not take relatives' medicines, including the sister's biotin or the mother-in-law's tablets
Reduce heavy carton lifting if possible, keep walking, and avoid staying in bed all day
Get seen the same day if unable to pass urine, if numbness stays, or if fever comes with much worse pain, and attend emergency if unable to pass urine

spec.situation: Manual worker or office worker with low back pain for 'a few weeks or since the move'; doctor asks about red flags (numbness, bladder, weight loss, fever) one by one; patient answers some clearly, some vaguely or with a story. Painkiller use mentioned.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Dose/frequency supported, but 500 mg is per tablet, not total dose.
bad.text: Panadol (generic_name=paracetamol, dose=500 mg, frequency=two tablets in the morning and two after work if the ache is up; sometimes skips the afternoon dose, indication=low back ache, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Chills were specifically asked about and denied along with fever/night sweats.
Doctor stated that there were no red flags for cauda equina, infection, or other sinister cause.
